title: Free AI Video With a Google Account: What Gemini Omni 1.1 in Google Vids Does, and the Real Quota
description:
Google Vids now lets any Google account generate AI video for free with Gemini Omni 1.1. This video shows how to make a clip, and covers five things the announcement doesn't make clear and how Google's help pages answer them.
For anyone who wants to make video with AI without paying or learning to edit.

Covers: making a clip on desktop, inserting it into a Vid before you close the tab, Chinese prompts and the age requirement, whether phones can generate, region limits on uploaded video, when the new AI voiceover goes live; why the two help pages give different quotas, the SynthID watermark, and "for use only within Vids". This site did not test how well it generates.

chapters.what-is: What Is Google Vids AI Video
chapters.how-to: Make a Free AI Video in Vids

wchu.text: This free AI video tool has five things Google's announcement doesn't spell out.

gqa7.text: You may think "free" in the announcement covers everything.

chza.text: It doesn't say if Chinese prompts work, or if phones can make one.

yvre.text: Answers are on official pages; I gathered them.

5wgf.text: It's the AI video feature in Google Vids.

ezrk.text: The model behind it is Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash.

ueaj.text: Google says it's free, and anyone can use it.

rkgw.text: The headline: anyone can make high-quality video.

7kht.text: The body adds one more line.

8p6r.text: With a Google or Workspace account: free.

gjup.text: So how do you actually make one?

dfmy.text: Google's help page gives five steps.

uhab.text: Step one: on a computer, open the Vids URL.

rrkk.text: Step two: start screen, Create AI videos.

9i94.text: Step three: write a prompt with subject, place, action and camera.

qfwd.text: Step four: choose landscape or portrait, and 3 to 10 seconds.

skjm.text: First time, practice on a simple scene.

csj2.text: Google's help page says to add dialogue, sound and tone.

fe7c.text: A prompt of just "a beautiful beach video" is too vague, so the model guesses.

nz9d.text: Swap in dusk, a dog, a low-angle tracking shot, warm light and wave sounds: far more specific.

rnw8.text: My view: a prompt is like telling a cinematographer the shots.

ikef.text: Personal accounts get preset avatars only, no custom ones.

24vb.text: Avatars as clip material: English-only, listed plans only; check eligibility.

xfxp.text: Ten seconds is short; new controls help make longer ones.

9meb.text: First, extend a scene; Google says lighting and characters stay consistent.

xep9.text: Second, set exact seconds to match story and narration.

r44r.text: Third, generate in Full HD or upgrade old clips.

krnz.text: My view: only watching the extended clip tells you if it looks good.

33ji.text: After each clip, don't skip one step.

hsue.text: The history exists only in this session.

itua.text: Close the tab and the clips you just made are gone.

s7f6.text: So after making one, insert it into your own Vid; that saves it.

tred.text: The help page says that to edit or use it later, insert it into a Vid first.

n9n5.text: Get in the habit: like it, insert it.

mrxt.text: Those are the steps. So what did the announcement leave unclear?

xi4n.text: Five items; official answers are on the right.

mksp.text: Fourth: region limits for uploaded videos.

hqkj.text: Fifth: when the new AI voiceover goes live.

qfzs.text: Glance at the answers; details one by one.

tnsk.text: Can you write prompts in Chinese?

7xnu.text: Official answer: the language table lists no AI video; unlisted features are English only.

ixne.text: The page links a language table.

vzju.text: The table has images, voiceover and avatars; features missing from it are marked English only.

3gje.text: Official advice: if a feature is English-only, switch your account language to English.

jx22.text: Second: is there an age requirement?

fsf9.text: The Gemini getting-started page that generation links to says you must be 18 or older.

nrat.text: Official steps all start on desktop Vids.

chsh.text: Vids' getting-started page: on phones you can only view, not edit.

g9ei.text: Fourth: editing uploaded videos has region limits.

pcqq.text: Also not in Illinois or Texas in the US.

nqbw.text: The usage page only says: wherever Workspace is offered.

tjxx.text: Uploads over 10 seconds: only the last 10 seconds are edited.

cysz.text: Announcement: Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite text-to-speech, coming soon.

bp5e.text: It says it will cover 100+ languages.

u2gj.text: September 29: an update says it's live, for listed plans only.

jm3a.text: Where it's silent, the practical way is checking your own screen.

radj.text: The usage page says to sign in to the right Google account first.

p83d.text: Without the feature, the start screen won't show it.

y76w.text: On work or school accounts, an admin can also turn generative AI off.

263x.text: And for what the official pages do state, does every page say the same?

iyr4.text: Who can use it: the three pages differ.

cdjf.text: Announcement: Google or Workspace account, free.

ifi6.text: Help page starts: needs an eligible Workspace subscription.

cyxg.text: The usage page gives personal accounts their own quota row.

itx5.text: Quotas: the two pages side by side.

3x75.text: The generation help page says most users get up to 50 videos a month.

i84s.text: Usage page, personal: 6 clips a month, shared with avatars.

us6x.text: Row one, the generation page: most users get 50 videos a month.

jdpm.text: Row two, the usage page's personal account: 6 clips, shared with avatars.

evm7.text: Both rows say it resets monthly on the 1st at midnight Pacific.

bgex.text: Row three, the default when the usage page sets no other limit: 500 seconds.

yuft.text: Different accounts and units: can't compare directly.

pesn.text: My way: pick no single number, check in these three steps.

artk.text: Step one: confirm your account type.

3z47.text: Step two: find your row on the usage page; clips or seconds?

xii4.text: Step three: sign in and read the quota shown.

z9hj.text: Google also says quotas and features may change later.

7b7c.text: Both pages' wording and all limits are in the article on the description's first line.

ta5k.text: And where can you actually use what you make?

9t34.text: A line at the page bottom.

ynjh.text: It says: "Generated images and videos are for use only within Vids."

mcdr.text: The page doesn't say whether this applies to exported videos.

yw2i.text: Before reuse elsewhere, read the usage policy.

vrq8.text: First, you must follow Google's Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy.

t46a.text: Google also warns content may not reflect real-world situations.

vavj.text: SynthID: hidden watermark on all clips.

w386.text: Google says it lets people check if content is AI-made.

vvpv.text: My view: a watermark doesn't mean you meet countries' AI labeling rules.

xtsm.text: After all this, is this free tool worth trying?

jzhk.text: Worth trying? My view: make one clip first, but remember three things.

nkvm.text: First, insert it into a Vid.

7d88.text: Second: trust your account's quota, not others'.

qqjw.text: Third: officially it's for use within Vids only, and watermarked.

i3s3.text: Also, you now have answers to the opening five.

3yjx.text: Chinese prompts: not in the language table, so English only.

ew36.text: Upload editing: not in some places.

y9fj.text: New AI voiceover: the September 29 update says it's live, listed plans only.

ri3w.text: This is official wording only; I haven't tested the output.

knpp.text: Quotas and usage scope: go by the latest official pages.

xqza.text: Full write-up: the article on the description's first line.

cmwf.text: Free is true, but knowing those five things before you start saves wasted work.
